Refs #6614. Split out of #6637, which keeps the delete-path fixes. This PR is only the one-off cleanup of the orphans those leaks left behind.

## Migration — `1790800000000-CleanUpOrphanedRecordsAndPolicies`

One-off and **reversible**. It deletes, in this order:
1. classifications, licenses and profiles that nothing names; their cascading children go with them;
2. the locations and storage buckets owned by the profiles deleted in step 1;
3. every authorization policy that nothing names, including the ones freed by steps 1–2.

Policies go last on purpose. The issue allows any order, and going last also catches the policies that steps 1–2 free.

### Backups and `down()`

Every deleted row is copied whole into `_orphan_cleanup_backup_<table>`. The copy happens in the same SQL statement as the delete, and every part of that statement reads the database as it was before any row is deleted. Three things are copied:
- the row itself;
- the children Postgres deletes with it (tagset, reference, visual, license_entitlement);
- every reference to it that Postgres sets to NULL, kept in `_orphan_cleanup_backup_nulled_references`. Today the only such reference is `file.tagsetId`.

The backups stay in place until the fix is confirmed. `down()` then inserts the rows back parents first, restores each nulled reference that is **still NULL** (one that was set since is left alone), and drops the backup tables.

The backup tables are not counted as names, otherwise the copies would keep the rows they copy. If a table is backed up but missing from `RESTORE_ORDER`, `up()` throws, so `down()` can never silently skip a backup.

**Follow-up:** once the fix is confirmed, a later migration drops the `_orphan_cleanup_backup_*` tables. Only `down()` drops them today.

### Safeguards
- **A row is kept while anything names it:** any foreign key, or any column carrying its id under the conventional name. The migration backup tables, e.g. `_auth_profile_backup_*.profileId`, hold such columns without an FK. Only an explicit list of each table's own cascading children is ignored, so an unknown reference keeps the row, including an owner whose key cascades. If nothing names a table at all, the migration throws instead of deleting every row.
- **There is no generic bucket or location sweep.** The Matrix media staging bucket is named only from configuration (`storage.file_service.matrix_media_bucket_id`). Only buckets and locations whose profile this migration deleted are removed.
- **Files are never deleted.** Their content lives in file-service storage, which only file-service may release. An unowned profile whose bucket holds files is left whole and counted in the log.
- **Rows created in the last day are skipped,** so an in-flight create, which saves children before their parent, cannot lose a child.
- **Only deleted ids come back to Node** (plus a deleted profile's location and bucket ids). Whole rows go from the delete straight into the backup inside Postgres, so ~15k policies' rule JSON is never held in Node memory.

## Dry run on a full dev copy of acceptance data (`up()` → `down()`, rolled back)

| | deleted | after `down()` |
|---|---|---|
| classifications | 2,997 | byte-identical |
| licenses / entitlements | 12 / 106 | byte-identical |
| profiles / locations / storage buckets | 44 / 44 / 44 | byte-identical |
| tagsets / references / visuals | 2,918 / 25 / 13 | byte-identical |
| authorization policies | 15,396 | byte-identical |
| files | 0 | byte-identical |

`up()` took ~14 s. A second run deletes nothing. 12 unowned profile trees whose buckets hold files are left for a file-service cleanup.

Of the deleted classifications, 729 are the live leak since April; the rest are 2025 rows whose policy was never computed, with no owner.

## Tests
- `clean-up-orphaned-records-and-policies.postgres.spec.ts` (10 cases) runs in the CI PostgreSQL job via `pnpm run test:migration:orphan-cleanup:postgres`, which fails rather than skips when `MIGRATION_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset. One case runs `up()` then `down()` and expects every table to come back byte-identical, including a nulled `file.tagsetId`. Removing any one safeguard turns a specific case red; so do dropping the nulled-reference capture and dropping the backup-table exclusion.

## Deploy notes
- Rollback: `migration:revert` restores the deleted rows from the backup tables. The deploy pipeline's gated pre-migration backup remains the last resort.
- Independent of #6637 in either order. Until #6637 ships, the delete paths keep leaking, so some orphans will reappear after this runs.

## Not in this PR
- The policy leaks of the group-A delete paths and failed creates.
- File-bearing orphan trees, historical empty orphan buckets (the 813 in the issue), and orphaned aggregators/documents: these need a file-service path.
- Dropping the backup tables (follow-up, above).

Fixes #6536.

## What went wrong

Every conversion and move mutation is gated on an in-memory policy built in the `ConversionResolverMutations` constructor. Its role list is the entire check — the policy is in-memory, so no credential rule in the database can widen it.

`67bc7945f` ("initial pass at updating global roles", May 2024) renamed the global role `global-admin-spaces` to `global-support`. Throughout that commit the symbol was renamed in place and kept in its lists:

```diff
-  AuthorizationCredential.GLOBAL_ADMIN_SPACES,
+  AuthorizationCredential.GLOBAL_SUPPORT,
```

At this one call site it was deleted instead of renamed:

```diff
-    [
-      AuthorizationRoleGlobal.GLOBAL_ADMIN,
-      AuthorizationRoleGlobal.GLOBAL_ADMIN_SPACES,
-    ],
+    [AuthorizationRoleGlobal.GLOBAL_ADMIN],
```

Holders of the role now called `global-support` silently lost access to all seven mutations sharing this policy: `convertSpaceL1ToSpaceL0`, `convertSpaceL2ToSpaceL1`, `convertSpaceL1ToSpaceL2`, `moveSpaceL1ToSpaceL0`, `moveSpaceL1ToSpaceL2`, `moveSpaceL2ToSpaceL1`, `convertVirtualContributorToUseKnowledgeBase`.

It reads as a rename that missed a call site rather than a deliberate restriction — nothing in that commit suggests an intent to narrow conversions. **If the narrowing was intentional, this PR should be closed and #6536 answered instead**; I could not find anything recording that intent.

## What this changes

Restores `GLOBAL_SUPPORT` to the role list, and adds a test asserting the list. Nothing covered it before, which is exactly why the rename went unnoticed — the existing specs mock `grantAccessOrFail`, so they pass whatever the roles are.

This also realigns the gate with `createPlatformCredentialRules`, which grants `PLATFORM_ADMIN` to `global-admin`, `global-support` and `global-license-manager`. Before this change a caller could hold `PLATFORM_ADMIN` on the platform and still be refused here.

## Verification

- `vitest run conversion.resolver.mutations.spec.ts` — 20 passed.
- Negative control: reverting the one-line source change fails the new test with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ [ 'global-admin', …(1) ], …(2) ]`, so it does guard the regression.
- `biome check` clean on both files.

## Deliberately left out

Two things surfaced in #6536 that made this hard to diagnose but are separate changes:

- `global-license-manager` also holds `PLATFORM_ADMIN` platform-side but is not in this list. I have not added it — widening beyond restoring the lost role is a product call, not a regression fix.
- The failure logs `on authorization undefined of type 'in-memory'`, which reads like a missing policy and sends you looking in the database. The policy name is already passed to the constructor and would point straight at the real check.

Closes #6021

Related (remain open until manually closed): alkem-io/server#4970, alkem-io/client-web#9353.

Workspace spec: `workspace#063-callout-transfer-flow-state` — https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/feat/063-callout-transfer-flow-state/specs/063-callout-transfer-flow-state/

## What was still broken after #6339

QA re-tested #6021 after #6339 merged and acceptance criterion 3 ("same logic applies when the destination's innovation flow was changed via template", the alkem-io/client-web#9353 sequence) still failed: the transferred callout is tagged with one of the destination's **old** state names and shows on no flow tab.

## Root cause (proven at code level)

The transfer logic from #6339 is correct but validates against the destination's flow-state `TagsetTemplate` (`allowedValues` / `defaultSelectedValue`), and that template drifts from the `InnovationFlow`'s actual states through three writers:

1. **Template apply** — `updateCollaborationFromSpaceTemplate` loads the target collaboration with `calloutsSet.tagsetTemplateSet` (eager `tagsetTemplates`, `cascade: true` on every hop). `updateInnovationFlowStates` updates a *separately loaded* copy of the template and saves it; the applier's final `collaborationService.save(targetCollaboration)` then cascades the **stale** in-memory template back over the row, reverting `allowedValues`/`defaultSelectedValue` to the pre-template names. The destination's own callouts stay visible (they are re-homed by state *name*), which is why only transfers exposed it.
2. **Add / delete a single state** — neither `createStateOnInnovationFlow` nor `deleteStateOnInnovationFlow` ever rewrote the template.
3. **Rename** — `TagsetService.updateTagsetsSelectedValue` re-tagged callouts in memory on the rename branch and `continue`d without `save`; nothing cascades to those tagsets, so callouts in a renamed phase kept the old name on reload.

## Fix (behaviour-only; no DDL, no GraphQL change)

- `TemplateApplierService`: re-read the callouts set's `TagsetTemplateSet` after the flow-state update, so the cascade save persists the current vocabulary and template-added callouts are classified against it.
- `InnovationFlowService`: add/delete state rewrite the flow-state template; one shared default rule (`resolveDefaultFlowStateName`: current state while it exists, else first) now backs template apply, rename, add and delete.
- `TagsetService`: persist the re-tag on the rename branch.
- Migration `1789000000000-ResyncFlowStateTagsetTemplates` (data-only, idempotent, no-op `down`): re-derives `allowedValues` from the flow's states in flow order, repairs a missing/unknown default, and moves callout flow-state tags that match no state (case-insensitively) to that default. Existing drifted spaces (acceptance, where QA reproduced this) are healed on deploy.

## Regression tests (each RED on `develop`, GREEN here)

- `template.applier.service.spec.ts` — the #9353 sequence: the graph handed to the cascade save carries the template's new state names; template-added callouts see the updated vocabulary.
- `innovation.flow.service.spec.ts` — add-state (incl. sort-order insertion) and delete-state (incl. deleting the current state) rewrite the vocabulary with the shared default rule; two pins for the default rule on the template path.
- `tagset.service.spec.ts` — rename branch saves the re-tagged tagset.
- `src/migrations/__tests__/1789000000000-ResyncFlowStateTagsetTemplates.spec.ts` — structural pins (three ordered UPDATEs, idempotence guards, case-insensitive re-tag, no DDL, no-op down).
- #6339's transfer pins (`classification.service.spec.ts`, `callout.transfer.service.spec.ts`) unchanged and green.

Fixes alkem-io/server#6492

## Root cause

Memo signing renders the live Yjs projection and resolves every internal image through document metadata and file-service bytes. Existing memos can still reference a document whose metadata row is absent, or whose metadata exists while the backing bytes return a typed 404. The renderer correctly fails rather than silently changing the signed output, but the existing collaboration migration worker had no memo-image discovery or repair path.

## Fix

- extends the existing one-shot collaboration migration worker with `--repair-memo-images --actor-id <uuid>`; it is a read-only dry run by default, and mutation requires explicit `--apply`
- reads each current memo through the live collaboration room, reports exact missing references and repeated occurrence counts, and only treats typed metadata absence or a typed file-service 404 as confirmed loss
- leaves authorization failures, transport failures/timeouts, 5xx responses, malformed responses, foreign-bucket metadata, and malformed internal locators untouched and reports the memo as failed
- removes only confirmed-missing image nodes from the fresh live Yjs document and persists via the existing correlated durability-barrier path, so concurrent edits are not overwritten by a stale snapshot
- preserves valid/external images and unrelated memo text, formatting, lists, and tables; rerunning a completed repair is a no-op
- reports visual loss explicitly, while the repaired projection is also the projection used by preview/signing

The memo image schema contains no alternate byte source to recover a genuinely absent internal document. Images whose metadata and non-empty file-service bytes are available are preserved.

- focused repair/CLI/module suite: 18 passed
- full `pnpm test:ci`: 793 files passed, 8 skipped; 9,247 tests passed, 28 skipped
- `pnpm build`: passed
- `pnpm lint` (TypeScript + Biome): passed
- commit hooks: full no-coverage test suite and typecheck passed

## What / why

A persona on the **generic** engine had no server-side route to receive a stored prompt graph: the invocation builder attached `promptGraph` only inside the `EXPERT` branch. So the declarative graph support merged in [virtual-contributor#122](https://github.com/alkem-io/virtual-contributor/pull/122) (conditional edges, retrieve/echo nodes, the shipped workshop payload) was live but **unreachable through configuration**.

This adds a `PROMPT_GRAPH_ENGINES` allowlist covering `expert` + `generic-openai`, new GraphQL authoring fields for the node/edge forms, an activation guide, and the workshop authoring fixture.

Closes #6385. Spec: `workspace#053-generic-prompt-graph`.

## What actually changed in production code

Most of the diff is tests and docs, but **three source files change existing behaviour** — worth reading rather than skimming:

**`ai.persona.resolver.mutations.ts` — the `aiServerUpdateAiPersona` body was restructured, not extended.** The fetch and the authorization check moved inside a `try`, an audit call was added on both the success and failure paths, and a constructor dependency was added. **The authorization check is unchanged in substance and still runs before any update**: same `grantAccessOrFail`, same `AuthorizationPrivilege.UPDATE`, same policy object, same position relative to the mutation — only its enclosing block moved. That is the property to verify when reviewing this hunk, and it is why the restructure is called out here instead of being described as an addition.

**`ai.persona.service.ts` — two conditions changed.** `input.engine === AiPersonaEngine.EXPERT` became `PROMPT_GRAPH_ENGINES.includes(input.engine)`; that is the feature. A second condition was *tightened*: `if (!invocationGraph)` became `if (!invocationGraph && input.engine === AiPersonaEngine.EXPERT)`, deliberately keeping the default-graph fallback expert-only so a generic persona with no stored graph produces **no `promptGraph` key at all** rather than inheriting expert's default.

**`prompt.graph.node.dto.ts` / `prompt.graph.edge.dto.ts` / `ai.persona.dto.update.ts`** add nullable fields; the only removal is an import line being widened.

Genuinely additive: every new test file, the docs, and the fixture. **No pre-existing test was modified or deleted** (`git diff origin/develop..HEAD -- '**/*.spec.ts' | grep -c '^-'` = 0), and the **GraphQL schema** delta is additive — 21 added, 0 breaking.

## Decisions worth reviewing

- **The story said "GENERIC"; there is no such enum value.** It is `AiPersonaEngine.GENERIC_OPENAI` (`generic-openai`) — the routing key bound to the `virtual-contributor-engine-generic` queue.
- **The allowlist deliberately excludes** `guidance`, `openai-assistant`, `libra-flow`, `community-manager`: widening requires engine-side graph execution first. A future enum value defaults to *not* attaching.
- **No validation of the graph/body-of-knowledge pairing.** `bodyOfKnowledgeID` is per-invocation from the VC, not stored on the persona, so the server cannot validate it. A retrieve-bearing graph on a BoK-less persona hard-fails at engine parse time and the member sees the standard error response — a documented precondition, not a defect.
- **No migration**: `ai_persona.promptGraph` jsonb already existed engine-independently.
- Expert behaviour is byte-identical in all three modes (stored / default / none).

Clicking or tapping the group's picture or name also opens Group settings. 1:1 chats have no menu. The Guidance chat keeps its own buttons.
- **Group avatar (#10378).** The avatar now fills the whole circle: halves for 2 other members, a half and two quarters for 3, quarters for 4, and from 5 on three faces plus "+N". The header, the list and the group settings dialog all show the same members, without the viewer.
- **Expand (#10266).** On desktop a new header button expands the chat to a large centered window (960×800 at most, with room left for the floating launcher) and collapses it back. Below the small breakpoint the chat is already full-screen, so the button is not shown there.
- **Scrolling (#10284).** Scrolling past the end of the conversation list or the thread no longer scrolls the page behind the chat. While the chat covers the page (expanded, or full-screen on mobile), the page does not scroll at all.

## Root causes
- Gear: `UnifiedChatPanelConnector` always passed `onGoToSettings`, so `ChatPanel` rendered the gear in every view.
- Avatar: `GroupAvatar` was a fixed 2×2 grid, so 2 members filled the top half and 3 left a quarter empty. The settings dialog was given the member list including the viewer, so it disagreed with the header and the list.
- No expand control existed. `ChatPanel` was a fixed 380×600 card.
- Scrolling: the panel is a plain non-modal `role="dialog"` div, not a Radix overlay, so no scroll lock applies to it. Its two scrollers had no `overscroll-behavior`, so a wheel or touch gesture reaching either end chained to the document. This was confirmed in Chromium. The Safari-only premise in the issue was not reproduced, because WebKit at desktop size cannot be driven headless here.

## Changes
- `ChatPanel`:
  - adds `onTitleClick` and `titleActionLabel`, which turn the avatar and title into one button whose accessible name is the title plus the action;
  - adds the expand/collapse toggle (desktop only), which swaps its accessible name, exposes `aria-expanded` and keeps focus;
  - while it covers the page, sets `overflow: hidden` on `<body>`, restoring the previous value on collapse, close or unmount.
- New CRD `ChatOptionsMenu` (Radix dropdown, tooltip, keyboard operable).
- `GroupAvatar` lays out by member count, plus a "+N" tile.
- The connector shows the gear in the list view only, uses the options menu, title action and leave confirmation for groups, and gives the settings dialog the same avatar members.
- `overscroll-contain` on the thread scroller and the conversation list.
- i18n: `panel.expand`, `panel.collapse` and `thread.options` in all six locales.
- Unit tests: `GroupAvatar`, `ChatOptionsMenu`, `ChatPanel` (header, expand, scroll lock), connector header wiring, and the two scrollers.

## Fixes after review and verification
A code review and a live verification run of this branch found two defects. Each is fixed in a new commit with a unit test that fails without it.
- **The page jumped to the top when a dialog opened over the expanded chat.**
  - Scroll the page down, open the chat, expand it, then open the ⋮ menu, Group settings or New message: the page jumped to `scrollY` 0 and stayed there after closing. It reproduced at desktop size and in the full-screen mobile chat.
  - Cause: the chat's lock set `overflow: hidden` on `<html>`, and Radix dialogs lock `<body>`. With `<html>` no longer `overflow: visible`, the body's overflow stops reaching the viewport, so the body clips itself to one screen height and the browser clamps the scroll to 0.
  - Fix: the chat locks `<body>`, the same element Radix locks, so the two locks combine.
- **The expand toggle did not expose its state.** It now has `aria-expanded`, as `src/crd/CLAUDE.md` requires for toggle buttons.

Live re-verification, two consecutive cycles on fresh data with the scripts of the run that found them. Every check passed in both cycles:
- **Page position:** with the page scrolled to 2000, the expanded chat open and the ⋮ menu, Group settings or New message opened and closed, the page stays at 2000 through collapse and close. The same holds in the full-screen chat on Pixel 7. Before the fix every one of these dropped to 0.
- **Expand toggle:** `aria-expanded` is `false` collapsed and `true` expanded.
- **Scroll containment:** page scrollY stays 0→0 when scrolling past the end of the list and the thread, in the small and the expanded window (3 runs each).
- **Regression baseline:** 11/11 in the small and the expanded window.

The evidence below was gathered before these fixes, when the lock was on `<html>`; the containment checks above repeat it with the lock on `<body>`.

## Evidence (live, isolated local stack, Chromium headless, Playwright 1.63)
Two consecutive passing cycles on fresh data (users A–E, conversations created by the scripts). Same method as the develop repro.

| Check | develop (before) | this branch (after, 2 cycles) |
|---|---|---|
| Scroll chaining, r08 method (1280×640, notifications page, 25×250px wheel at list/thread end) | page `scrollY` 0→2400 for list and thread, 3/3 | 0→0 for list and thread, 3/3 per cycle; both scrollers at their end, `overscroll-behavior: contain` |
| Expanded: wheel over header, composer, page margin, thread, list | n/a | `scrollY` 0→0 for all five, 3/3 per cycle; `<html>` overflow `hidden` while expanded |
| Small window: wheel on the page outside the chat | scrolls | still scrolls (0→2400), by design; also after collapse |
| Mobile Pixel 7 (touch), swipes on list, thread and both headers | not measured | page `scrollY` 0→0, 2/2 per cycle; scrolls again after closing (0→~800) |
| Gear | navigates away from a thread | thread header has none; list gear opens notification settings and closes the chat |
| Group avatar, A sees 2 / 3 / 4 others | 2: top half only; 3: one quadrant empty | halves / half + 2 quarters / quarters; tiles cover 100% of the circle; header identical to list; settings dialog same members |
| Expand | no control | 960×800 at 1440×900, 864×704 at 1024×768, centered, no overlap with the launcher or the send button; send, history scroll, draft, staged attachment and composer node survive collapse; Enter/Space toggle keeps focus |
| Baseline: 1:1 and group create/send/receive, add member, remove member | 11/11 | 11/11 in the small window and 11/11 in the expanded window, per cycle |

"+N", checked in two further consecutive cycles on fresh data with seven users: A in a group with 6 others shows three faces and "+3" in the bottom-right quarter. After one member is removed (5 others) it shows "+2". The layout is identical in the header, the conversation list and the group settings dialog, the tiles cover 100% of the circle, and the "+N" text fits inside its tile (16px quarter at the small size, 24px in the dialog; text 11×13px). The 11-step baseline passed in the small and the expanded window in both cycles.

## How to test
1. Open the chat list: there is a gear, and it opens notification settings. Open a 1:1 chat: there is no gear and no ⋮.
2. Open group chats with 2, 3, 4 and 5+ other members. Compare each header avatar with its list row. Hover ⋮ to see the "Chat options" tooltip. Use the keyboard to open the menu and choose Group settings. Click the group picture, then the name: both open Group settings. Use ⋮ → Leave group, cancel it, then confirm it on a throwaway group.
3. Desktop: expand the chat, send a message, scroll the history, start a draft with an attachment, then collapse: everything is still there. Repeat at about 1024×768 and check that nothing overlaps the launcher.
4. Scroll past the end of the list and of the thread: the page behind does not move. When expanded, scrolling anywhere does not move the page.
5. **Safari, before closing #10284:** on macOS Safari and on an iOS device (Safari), repeat step 4 in the small window and in the full-screen mobile chat, and drag on the chat header. The page behind must not scroll.

## Assumptions and open questions
- **The expanded window is non-modal:** no backdrop and no focus trap, the same element only resized. Toggling a Radix Dialog between modal and non-modal remounts its content, which would lose the scroll position and the staged attachments. Using `react-remove-scroll` directly would block scrolling inside portaled popovers such as the emoji picker. The page is still kept from scrolling while the chat covers it.
- **"Leave group" in the ⋮ menu comes from the prototype**, not from the designer's comment, which mentions only chat settings. Design should confirm.
- The `<body>` overflow lock also applies to the full-screen mobile chat, where the page behind is invisible.
- In a 1:1 chat the title click does nothing, because there are no per-chat settings yet.
- At the small size (32px) a quarter tile is 16px, so a two-digit "+NN" is tight. Initials in the half tiles are also crowded when members have no photo.
- Menu items render uppercase, consistent with the app's other menus and buttons.

- The composer textarea (shared `CommentInput`) still lets overscroll chain to the page in the small window. I left it alone because the component is shared beyond chat.

## ⚠️ MERGE ORDER IS A PREREQUISITE, NOT A PREFERENCE

**Merge and deploy alkem-io/server#6667 to the shared test cluster BEFORE merging this.**

`server-api/vitest.config.ts` puts `src/functional-api/callout/**` in the **`nightly`** project, which runs against the shared cluster. From the moment this file lands on `develop`, the nightly executes it — **fixture writes included** — and reports it red until the server slice is deployed there.

The remedy is merge order, not confinement: a "assert `ALKEMIO_SERVER` is localhost" pre-flight would red the nightly *by construction*, since the nightly deliberately targets the shared cluster. This is stated in the file's own header. If the order cannot be held, the nightly is **knowingly red** for this spec — and the slice contract forbids buying the window with a `skip`.

## Why this repo is in the feature at all

Because nothing else could prove the central claim. `vitest` runs `environment: 'node'` with hand-wired repository mocks and **no Postgres**, so every server unit assertion restates its own mock. `SC-002` requires the account boundary be exercised "against a real account boundary at least once" — this suite is that once, and it is the only place the SQL join is not restated by the thing testing it.

## The six cases

1. `AC4`/`FR-003` — a foreign-account id is **rejected on create**, nothing persisted
2. `AC4`/`FR-003b` — a **newly added** foreign id is rejected on update, the stored list untouched
3. `AC7` — an id that **left the account** is dropped silently, the save succeeds
4. `AC1`/`FR-004a`/`FR-017` — a cross-L0 same-account space **and** the host's own L2 are accepted, persisted, and the collection renders whole
5. `AC2`/`FR-010` — `accountSpaces` offers every level and **never** the foreign space
6. `AC3`/`FR-009` — `accountSpaces` is refused to an actor holding `READ` but not `UPDATE`

**Case 4 is the load-bearing one.** Every L1/L2 row's own `accountId` is NULL (`account` is assigned only at `SpaceLevel.L0`; `createSubspace` propagates `levelZeroSpaceID` and never touches `account`). So a predicate spelled `space."accountId" = <host account>` returns the empty set for the sibling L1, the write guard rejects it, and case 4 goes **red**. It passed twice — so the executed SQL must resolve the account through `levelZeroSpaceID`. That is the defect this suite exists to catch, disproven by execution rather than by reading code.

Verified: **6/6 passing, twice, exit 0**, against a stack carrying the server slice.

## Evidence

| Phase | Result |
|---|---|
| Triage | route `spec`; **3 of the issue's own premises refuted** |
| Spec | accepted after 3 attempts (21→13 blocking); net-subtractive |
| Build | 7 chunks green, cross-repo contract passed first round, simplifier −116 lines |
| Verify | it-spec **6/6 twice** (`SC-002` satisfied against real Postgres) · walks **US1 10/10, US2 3/3** |
| Review | 2 full funnel rounds + 1 scoped: 67 raw → 31 actionable → all fixed, 0 regressions |

**Verification highlights.** `AC1` proven with a genuine negative: the picker offered the host, its L1, its L2, a sibling L0 of the account and a subspace under it, while a space on a *different* account — one the admin provably holds `READ` on — never appeared under any query, so the scoping is by **account**, not by read access. `AC8` proven in its hardest form: with `selectedIds` holding a sibling L0 and a deep L2 but `mode: AUTO`, the collection still rendered only the host's own subspace, with no notice. Both `D3` regressions hold — `CUSTOM→AUTO→CUSTOM` preserves the stored selection, and an unrelated Contributors-callout edit leaves its contributor selection intact.

## What review caught that nothing else would have

- **`SEC-084-01`** — the account-wide SPACES selection was writable by a **non-admin**. The create path gates SPACES framing behind space-admin `CREATE`; the update path's "mirror" of that guard covered `CONTRIBUTORS` only. A plain member could create a POST callout (they hold `UPDATE` on their own callout, and `allowMembersToCreateCallouts` maps `CREATE_CALLOUT`→`CONTRIBUTE`), convert it to SPACES, and publish an account-portfolio-wide collection — the capability `AC3` reserves for a host-space admin. Fixed subtractively by routing the update path through the create path's own helper.
- **`SEC-084-CW-01`** — `AC6`'s privacy design was defeated on the same page: `selectedIds` was served to every viewer, so a non-member could diff it against the rendered `framing.subspaces` and recover the exact hidden **count** and the **UUIDs** withheld from them. Fixed in two places — GraphQL, and the MCP callout resource, which was emitting the entire raw `settings` jsonb under a READ-only gate reachable with an ordinary browser cookie.
- A **permanently-red test** added beyond its brief and auto-enrolled in the shared-cluster nightly — deleted.

## Open items for a human

- **`ac4-literal-wording` (open gate).** Built as A11: a *newly added* out-of-account id is **rejected**; a *carried-over* id that has left the account is **silently dropped** and the save succeeds. This resolves a real contradiction between `AC4` ("reject any") and `AC7` ("omitted on save") in `AC7`'s favour. The strict reading of `AC4` is purely **additive** on top if you want it.
- **Two refused severity downgrades.** The adjudicator argued `SEC-084-01` down to medium (curation, not exposure — the read path still filters per viewer) and `SEC-084-TS-01` down to low (30 existing specs already flip fixtures to PUBLIC in the nightly). Both were **refused and held** at the higher grade, because lowering a security grade is risk acceptance. Yours to grade.
- **`R-A` / `R-B` residuals, accepted by operator ruling 2026-10-14.** `R-A`: a host-space admin gains a publish surface over the account's whole portfolio with no account-level privilege. `R-B`: the identical rule is materially weaker on **organization** accounts, and account type is invisible at the point of use. Follow-up: alkem-io/alkemio#1847.
- **Recorded, not fixed** (both need a non-eager relation on a hot read path): a callout's **creator keeps `UPDATE` permanently** via `USER_SELF_MANAGEMENT`, so a demoted admin still reads the curated list; and Platform Support edits template callouts through a different privilege, so it reads `[]` and a read-modify-write would wipe the list (unreachable while the restricted-framing guard holds).
- **Pre-existing, filed as baseline:** `Account.spaces` is readable unfiltered by any viewer with `READ` on one space of the account; automatic mode still performs no list-level filtering and is exposed to the same whole-collection nullification. Neither is this feature's to fix — both deserve their own tickets.

## Honest caveats

- Four commits **postdate the full funnel review**: two received a scoped two-lane review, and the MCP narrowing plus its spec received full-suite + schema-gate + a RED-verified spec but no review lane. Both late changes are subtractive (a deleted guard, a narrowed payload).

## What changed

`server-api/src/functional-api/collabora/collabora-template-isolation.it-spec.ts`, four cases:

| case | asserts |
|---|---|
| **AC1** | the template carries the uploaded content — `documentType` derived from the file, hash equals the fixture |
| **AC2** | two posts from one template ⇒ **three distinct** backing fileIDs, all hashing to the fixture. One apply as `SPACE_ADMIN`, one as `SPACE_MEMBER` |
| **AC3** | writing to post A1 changes **only** A1 — the template's and A2's bytes are unchanged from values captured *before* the write |
| **AC6** | a foreign source is refused, naming the source (not the licence error, not a destination denial), and the callouts set is unchanged |

AC2's `SPACE_MEMBER` leg is the load-bearing one: it is the first proof that the new in-service source READ reaches a template-owned `CollaboraDocument` under `{roles: []}` authorization for an ordinary space role. A refusal there would have meant the feature was dead for every non-admin user (spec R-5, now **resolved**).

Every hash is compared against `fixtureHash(<file on disk>)`, never against a hash re-derived from another served response, and the byte reader asserts `Buffer.isBuffer` before hashing — without that guard a dropped superagent parser makes `res.body` `{}` and **every** comparison passes for the wrong reason.

Runs the nightly `server-api` suite in parallel — **79.2 min → 44.5 min (~1.8×)**, measured on `test-alkem.io` — without weakening a single assertion. All 108 files still run; nothing is skipped,
  deleted or quarantined to gain speed.

  `workspace#040-parallel-nightly-server-api` · story #570

  ## How it works

  The 108-file `nightly` project becomes two projects in the **same** config, run as **one** invocation: `nightly-parallel` (94 files, `groupOrder: 0`, `maxWorkers` from `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS`) and
  `nightly-serial` (14 files, `groupOrder: 1`, `maxWorkers: 1`). Sequential groups give lane separation without a second config or a report merge. The legacy `nightly` project is left **byte-untouched**
  as the rollback surface — reverting is one line in `package.json`.

  Lane membership is **derived, never hand-maintained**: a guard applies hazard rules with name-scoped transitive taint, proves the two lanes partition the nightly scope exactly, and fails closed on
  drift. New spec files default to serial until proven safe — which is how two specs that arrived from `develop` mid-flight were classified with no manual step.

  Three mechanisms protect the signal: **serial-confirm** (any parallel failure is re-run at one worker, and the *serial* verdict is the job's exit code; parallel-fail/serial-pass is logged as
  interference and demotes a file after ≥2 in 7 nights), the **lane guard**, and a **retrospective baseline diff**.

  ## The main finding

  Four static-analysis passes added rules and demoted 22 files, and each run still found interference the rules missed. Two runs on identically fresh databases gave **7 and 63 failures** — same code, same
  data. Every one adjudicated as interference, never a real defect.

  The hazardous pattern is *"assert a shared pool user's privileged action succeeds"* — most of the suite, and not soundly detectable statically. The server compounds it: the `ActorContext` cache is keyed
  by actor alone and **deleted** on any credential change for that actor anywhere.

  So the sharing was removed. **Each vitest worker now gets its own 13 identities** (slot from `VITEST_POOL_ID`; worker 0 keeps bare addresses, worker N uses plus-addressing). Under `pool: 'threads'` a
  worker runs one file at a time, so two concurrently-executing files **cannot** resolve the same identity — structural, not heuristic. On `test-alkem.io` a full run then came back **`exit=0`, 108/108 
  files, 2003 passed, zero failures**.

  This needed a non-obvious fix: `GLOBAL_ADMIN` is granted by the server's bootstrap against the literal `admin@alkem.io`, so per-worker admins were unprivileged and every global-admin scenario failed
  `FORBIDDEN_POLICY`. The harness now grants platform roles per slot at startup using worker 0's bootstrap-privileged token.

  ## Teardown was silently broken

  `cleanUpBaseScenario` wrapped its whole delete sequence in **one** `try`, so the first failure skipped every delete after it. And `deleteOrganization` fails while the account still hosts anything — with
  the org **last**, that failure was invisible. An organisation leaked on essentially every run, of every suite using the factory.

  Measured: wall-clock rose **20.5 → 28.7 min across six consecutive runs**, then dropped straight back to 21.1 when the database was recreated. **~36% of runtime was accumulated residue** — larger than
  every optimisation here combined.

  Teardown is now per-entity best-effort and enumerates what the account still hosts, deleting in the required order (L2 → L1 → L0 → VCs → packs → org). Verified behaviourally: the organisation is
  genuinely gone afterwards, including when an untracked resource was created under its account.

  ## Also here

  - **`uploads.it-spec.ts` is green** — long red because an organisation profile's first visual is an AVATAR, aspect-ratio-locked to 1:1, and the fixture was 410×256. The server was right; the fixture was
  stale.
  - **Environment allowlist guard** — refuses to provision identities against an unapproved host. The Kratos *admin* path bypasses the mail-verification step assumed to protect acc/prod, and this branch
  grows the pool to 13×W accounts with programmatic `GLOBAL_ADMIN`.
  - **Playwright traces no longer published publicly** — one published trace held 73 `ory_kratos_session` entries. They now go to a private 14-day artifact; screenshots and the summary still publish.
  - **Fail-loud worker sizing** — an oversized `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS` aborts naming the variable instead of silently halving the run and reporting green.
  - **Honest mint gate** — it had come to derive its expectation from the code path it polices; now also asserts an independent ceiling, so a duplicate mint can't hide.
  - **Skips never fail the build** — skipped/todo were recorded as failures, so ~59 phantom regressions would have appeared nightly once enforcement was enabled.
  - **Skips must cite a bug** — of 49 unconditional skips, 26 already did; the other 23 are on a closed, dated allowlist that new skips can't join and that fails when an entry goes stale.

  ## Evidence

  | Config | Environment | Wall-clock | Failures | Verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Baseline (CI, W=1) | test-alkem.io | 79.2 min | 2 | — |
  | 69/39, W=5 | test-alkem.io | 56.1 min | 0 | PASS |
  | **94/14, W=5** | **test-alkem.io** | **44.5 min** | 4, all interference | **PASS** |

  `W=10` was tried and failed — setup timeouts and mass-skipped files, one taking 602 s. Resource exhaustion, not interference. **W=5 is the operating point.**

  **client-web verified**: run from this branch against the same environment, it matched the `develop` baseline exactly — 279 tests, 270 passed, 0 failed, the same 2 flaky files, 7 skipped, `exit=0`. That
  exercises the teardown rewrite across its 68 scenario-using files. Its identity path is provably unchanged (`workerCount` defaults to 1; `VITEST_POOL_ID` is never set under Playwright, so slot 0 and
  bare addresses).

  ## Known limits

  - **Notification throughput is a real ceiling.** Parallelism multiplies it roughly linearly with workers; four suites in one day backed up RabbitMQ enough to take the notifications service down.
  - **More server pods will not help** — latency measured identical at rest and under full load; the server idles while the suite runs. The remaining lever is proximity (~43–50 ms RTT from a laptop vs
  ~0.1 ms local). Traefik overhead measured ~0.1 ms.
  - Hazard rules are name/shape blocklists, not structural proofs.
  - The teardown leak summary is **per-worker**, not whole-run — a `worker_threads` consequence; CI greps the whole log.

  - #608 — test data not reliably cleaned up.
  - Two diagnosed, unfixed server races: the `ActorContext` cache keying, and the conversion service's empty-roleSet window. Both recorded in the spec.

Promotes the unified-collaboration e2e from an uncommitted debugging `.mjs` into the `test-suites` standard `functional-e2e` structure as a **committed, CI-gating** suite covering **both memo and whiteboard** (epic `003-unify-collab-yjs`, SC-009 / WS-F).

## Approach — service level (protocol/backend)

Two raw `y-websocket` clients per document open `ws://localhost:3000/collab/<id>?type=<memo|whiteboard>` carrying the admin OIDC/BFF session cookie on the handshake, exchanging Yjs sync + awareness. **No React/ProseMirror/Excalidraw UI.** The whiteboard test mirrors the `@alkemio/excalidraw-yjs-binding` Yjs scene schema (`elements`/`files`/`appState`, per-property nested `Y.Map`) **without importing it** — it tests the WS/CRDT layer, not the binding.

The OIDC/BFF login (one short-lived Playwright Chrome → `alkemio_session` cookie) is extracted into a reusable helper and shared by both specs.

## Scenarios & assertions

**Memo** (`memo-collaboration.spec.ts`):
- CRDT convergence A → B
- Awareness / presence
- Persistence round-trip *(opt-in, see below)*

**Whiteboard** (`whiteboard-collaboration.spec.ts`):
- Convergence A → B
- **Per-property merge (headline)** — A edits `element.x`, B edits the **same** element's `strokeColor` concurrently → **both survive on both clients, NOT last-write-wins**; untouched props intact
- Awareness / presence
- Persistence round-trip *(opt-in)*

## Files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `collab/collab-auth.ts` | OIDC/BFF admin login → cookie + cookie-authed GraphQL |
| `collab/collab-fixture.ts` | `createMemoFixture` / `createWhiteboardFixture` via GraphQL |
| `collab/collab-ws.ts` | raw-WS Yjs client + `waitForDoc` / `waitForAwareness` |
| `collab/memo-collaboration.spec.ts` | memo scenarios |
| `collab/whiteboard-collaboration.spec.ts` | whiteboard scenarios |
| `collab/README.md` | scenarios, headless-vs-live, run instructions |

- New **`Collaboration`** project in `config/playwright.config.nightly.ts` (runs via `pnpm run test:nightly`).
- Adds `yjs` / `y-websocket` / `y-protocols` / `lib0` / `ws` (+ `@types/ws`) to `client-web` so `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` provides them in CI (lockfile updated).

## Proven headless now vs. live-only

Against the running local dev stack:
- ✅ **Deterministic / gating**: convergence, **per-property merge**, awareness — both memo and whiteboard. Default run: **2 passed / 2 skipped (18s)**.
- ⚠️ **Opt-in / non-gating**: the **persistence cold-rehydrate** assertions. The round-trip works intermittently but the cold client occasionally closes `1006` before the blob / `collaboration-fetch` flush completes, so enforcing it would flake CI. Skipped by default with a reason; run with `COLLAB_ASSERT_PERSISTENCE=true`. Enable once the persistence path is reliable.

## Requires (to execute)

The local dev stack must be up: gateway `localhost:3000` → unified collaboration service + server BFF (forward-auth + OIDC login). Tests scaffold fully and lint/typecheck without it; the live assertions need it.
